description: A recurring report said restricted-mode agents fail through the egress proxy and 'the plain-HTTP body framing is suspect' (IP upstream 502, hostname upstream reaches nginx but 408). Measured against the real startProxy with bun 1.3.14, a raw-socket client and a local echo upstream: GET absolute-URI 200 (upstream saw 'GET /echo'); POST with Content-Length, body in one write 200 (5B read); POST body split across two writes 200 (5B); POST chunked 200 (5B); GET again after a POST 200 (no poisoning). bun test src/proxy/server.test.ts -> 18 pass. By code: forwardHttp (src/proxy/server.ts:279-316) forwards host+content-length verbatim and pipes the body; matchAllowedDomain (:59) is a hostname suffix match so an IP literal can only ever produce 403 - never 502; grep for 408 across src/ returns zero hits, so the observed 408 did not originate in burrow.
resolution: Check configuration before code: the run's allowed_domains (burrow.toml sandbox.allowed_domains -> src/runner/dispatch.ts:206) and whether the requested host literal is routable from the host netns. Sandbox networking is already correct-shaped: bwrap --unshare-all then --share-net when network=open or restricted+proxyAddress (src/provider/local/bwrap.ts:62-64), with HTTP_PROXY/http_proxy set to proxy.url (dispatch.ts:216-218).

name: When a wrapped HTTP proxy 'drops bodies', validate the probe before the product
description: Two of my own probe harnesses reported that burrow's proxy never reached the upstream and closed the client socket at ~12s - which looked like a real defect and fitted a pre-existing hypothesis. Both were harness artifacts: recording the upstream request only on the 'end' event hides 'headers arrived, body never came', and a first probe's stalled case left every later request in the same process unanswered. A clean ordered probe (GET, POST single-write, POST two-write, POST chunked, GET-after-POST) plus the project's own test file passing 18/18 settled it in minutes.
